chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from his father Sulayman who said:

I was in the mosque when Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) entered, and I did not recognize him. So I asked about him and was informed of his name. Then I and others arose toward him, surrounded him, and greeted him.

A man then said to him: 'May Allah keep you well! What is your view regarding a man who names a specific woman and says on the day he marries her, she is divorced three times, then later changes his mind and wishes to marry her — is that permissible for him?' He said: 'Divorce is only after marriage.'

key_terms.الطلاق: Talaq — divorce; the formal unilateral repudiation of a wife by a husband
key_terms.النكاح: Nikah — the marriage contract; the formal Islamic marriage
key_terms.بعينها: By her very self/specifically — referring to a specific named individual, not a generic description
key_terms.طالق: Taliq — the passive participle meaning 'divorced/repudiated'; a specific legal status

ai.seo_question: Is a divorce pronounced before marriage valid in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question posed to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-'Abidin (AS) in the mosque. A man asked whether a pre-marital declaration of triple divorce is valid. The Imam's decisive ruling — 'divorce is only after marriage' — establishes a foundational principle of Islamic family law: a divorce uttered before a marriage is contracted has no legal effect and does not invalidate a subsequent marriage to that woman.
